course: AP Physics C: Electricity & Magnetism, all five units, derived rather than quoted — every formula the course hands a student is produced here from the law it comes out of, on a lightning research station where each one is a measurement somebody has to take
curriculum: Charge, and where it sits on a conductor
The electric field as a vector field, and field lines
Gauss's law, and choosing a surface it can be used on
Field of a charged sheet, line and sphere
Field inside a conductor, and shielding
Field enhancement at a point, and why height and radius both matter
Electric potential as a line integral of the field
Potential and field as derivative and integral of one another
Equipotentials, and what they mean on the ground
Capacitance as a ratio, before it is a formula
Parallel plates: capacitance from the field between them
Dielectrics, dielectric strength and breakdown
Energy stored in a capacitor, and where the half comes from
Capacitors in series and parallel
Current as a flow, and current density
Resistance, resistivity and the ground as a resistor
Kirchhoff's rules on a real network
The RC circuit, and what a time constant means
Instrument bandwidth: what a slow instrument cannot see
Magnetic field of a current, and Ampère's law
Biot–Savart, and when the integral is worth doing
Force on a current in a field, and forces between conductors
Magnetic flux through a surface
Faraday's law: an EMF from a changing flux
Lenz's law, and the sign that says which way
Mutual inductance: one circuit talking to another
Self-inductance, and why a straight wire has it
The LR transient, and inductive volts against resistive volts
Energy in the magnetic field, and where a strike puts it
Measurement in the right regime: shunts, dividers and what they load

equations.about: Gauss's law — flux out of a closed surface counts the charge inside it
symbols: the electric field, in volts per metre
an element of the closed surface, pointing outward
the charge inside that surface, in coulombs
the permittivity of free space, 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m

equations.about: the field of a charged layer, which does not fall off with distance
symbols: field between the layer and the ground, in volts per metre
charge per unit area on the layer, in coulombs per square metre

equations.about: potential difference as the work done along a path
symbols: the potential difference between two points, in volts
an element of the path taken between them

equations.about: parallel-plate capacitance, from the field between the plates
symbols: the area facing across the gap, in square metres

equations.about: the energy it took to charge it, and where the half comes from
Ampère's law — circulation of B counts the current through the loop
symbols: an element of a closed path
the current passing through that path, in amperes
the permeability of free space, 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A

equations.about: the field around a long straight conductor
symbols: field at distance r, in tesla
current in the conductor, in amperes
distance from its axis, in metres

equations.about: flux through a loop lying beside a conductor
symbols: magnetic flux through the loop, in webers
the length the loop runs parallel to the conductor, in metres
the near side's distance from it

equations.about: Faraday's law, and the sign that says which way
symbols: the flux through the loop, in webers

equations.about: the volts across an inductance, and why a straight lead has one
symbols: the voltage across the lead, in volts
its self-inductance, in henries — about a microhenry per metre for a straight wire
how fast the current through it is changing, in amperes per second

equations.about: the RC discharge, and the time constant that comes out of it
symbols: the charge left on the capacitor at time t
the resistance it discharges through, in ohms
